title: The invisible server
intro: You built a new weather server and the chatbot can't see its tools. The research, filesystem and fetch tools all work fine. Open the clues and diagnose.

facts.label: The server, standalone
facts.value: Run directly with the MCP inspector, weather_server.py connects, lists both its tools, and executes them perfectly.

facts.label: server_config.json
facts.value: Entries present: research, filesystem, fetch. Nothing else.

facts.label: The chatbot's startup log
facts.value: "Connected to server: research (2 tools), filesystem (11 tools), fetch (1 tool)." Three sessions opened, no errors, no mention of weather.

facts.label: The LLM's behaviour
facts.value: Asked about the weather, the model apologizes that it has no weather tool — it never attempts a call.

facts.label: The code
facts.value: MCP_ChatBot iterates the config file and opens one session per entry. It has no other discovery mechanism.

question: Why can't the chatbot see the weather tools?
choices: The weather server has a bug in its tool schemas
The server was never added to server_config.json — no entry, no session, no tools
stdio transport can't handle more than three servers
The LLM doesn't support weather-related tool calls
debrief: The inspector run proves the server itself is healthy — schemas list, tools execute. The startup log shows exactly three sessions, matching exactly three config entries, and the code's only discovery mechanism is iterating that file. The model never attempts a call because the tool list the client aggregated simply doesn't contain weather tools. One JSON entry — command, args — and the tools appear. The general lesson: in a config-driven multi-server client, absence from the config is silent; check registration before debugging servers.
